purpose: Single machine-readable registry of the sources that a GitHub Pages deployment builds or ships. It drives scripts/validate_deployment.mjs and is the only place where deployment roles, expected spatial scope, integrity guardrails, per-source analytical scope and the five-field source-freshness contract are declared. It deliberately contains no individual map records.
contract_1_1_0_note: 1.1.0 is additive and clarifying over 1.0.0. It adds two things per source and no analytical values. (1) An enumerated analytical `scope` — WHAT A SOURCE VALUE MEANS geometrically — defined in spatial_scopes.analytical_scopes. This is distinct from expected_spatial_scope, which is and remains a loose integrity bounding box for build validation; the two concepts are never merged. (2) A five-field freshness contract per source: reference_date, published_at, retrieved_at, update_frequency, source_state (with optional observed_cadence). Every non-null temporal value traces to a publisher statement or to repository evidence; none is inferred. A missing publisher date is written as an explicit null, never back-filled from another date. The catalogue record's 'Fecha de actualización' is never written into reference_date or published_at. The 1.0.0 fields (source_period_exposed_by_source, source_period_semantics, expected_spatial_scope, integrity_guardrail, interpretation_ceiling, ...) are retained unchanged so existing consumers keep working.
guardrail_note: Every min_count in this file is an ENGINEERING guardrail against an ingestion collapse (a truncated download, a schema change, an upstream outage that still returns parseable JSON). It is not a tourism indicator, not a threshold with analytical meaning, and not a claim about how many museums, stations or hotels Madrid has. Each value is set far below the count actually observed at calibration so that legitimate source change passes and only an obvious collapse fails. baseline_count and calibrated_on are recorded so a reviewer can see the headroom; changing a min_count is a visible diff and must be justified in the pull request that changes it.

spatial_scopes.analytical_scopes_note: The entries under analytical_scopes are the closed enum of ANALYTICAL scopes (what a value means), each source declares exactly one as its `scope`. The sibling entries that carry lat/lon bounds (madrid_city_area, central_madrid_area, madrid_city_and_surroundings_feed_area) are INTEGRITY ENVELOPES referenced by `expected_spatial_scope`; they are a different concept and the two must never be merged. Planning scopes (PLANNING_AMBITO, EXECUTION_UNIT, DEVELOPMENT_STAGE_AREA, PARCEL, ADDRESS_POINT, WORK_GEOMETRY, LENS_INTERSECT_AMBITO) are defined because Gate K authorised the enum; no planning production evidence ships until Gate L closes.

LENS_CIRCLE.definition: A user-positioned circle (100 m to 5 km). A value counted or measured inside the circle; it is user state, never a source-native geometry.

OFFICIAL_BARRIO.definition: One of the 131 current-era official barrio polygons. A value that belongs to the whole barrio and is never apportioned to a part of it.

OFFICIAL_DISTRICT.definition: One of the 21 official district polygons. A value that belongs to the whole district.

MUNICIPALITY.definition: The municipality of Madrid, INE code 28079. A citywide value describing no district, barrio or Lens circle.

POINT_OBSERVATION.definition: A single located record or reading at a point — a counter, sensor, station, asset or register entry. The value describes that point, not an area; it is never interpolated between points.

BOUNDED_STUDY_AREA.definition: An explicit bounded study-area polygon (e.g. the HATI pilot rectangle). Boundary context only; point-bounded evidence inside it keeps its own POINT_OBSERVATION scope.

PLANNING_AMBITO.definition: One whole official planning ambito of the PGOUM 97 planning instrument, identified by its exact official code. Every value at this scope describes the WHOLE ambito and is never apportioned, area-weighted or population-weighted into a Lens circle, a barrio, a district or any sub-area. Shipped by #68 (K6) under the Gate L source contract.

EXECUTION_UNIT.definition: An execution unit (UE) sub-area of a planning ámbito. Deferred; defined but unused.

DEVELOPMENT_STAGE_AREA.definition: A development-stage polygon (e.g. south-east development etapas). Deferred; defined but unused.

PARCEL.definition: A single cadastral/planning parcel polygon. Deferred; defined but unused.

ADDRESS_POINT.definition: An official address point resolved via the callejero (NDP). Shipped by #71 (K9): the granted-urban-licence layer and its callejero NDP crosswalk. A value at this scope describes one located record; it is counted inside a Lens circle and is never apportioned, aggregated into a barrio-level figure, ranked by area, or rendered as a density surface.

WORK_GEOMETRY.definition: A public-work geometry. Not adopted; defined but unused.

LENS_INTERSECT_AMBITO.definition: The MEMBERSHIP relation between a Lens circle and the planning ambitos it touches: it answers WHICH ambitos a circle touches and carries no ambito quantity, no overlap area, no overlapping fraction and no weight. It never answers what share of an ambito's published state, surface or available buildability lies inside the circle. Shipped by #68 (K6).

madrid_city_area.note: Generous box around the municipality of Madrid. Deliberately loose: its job is to catch null-island coordinates, swapped lat/lon, projected coordinates leaking through unconverted, and a source returning a different city — not to assert an administrative boundary.

central_madrid_area.note: Generous box around the app's central-Madrid envelope (40.385-40.455 N, -3.745 to -3.645 E). Looser than the envelope on purpose: the CRTM station query uses esriSpatialRelIntersects, so a station sitting on the boundary can be returned marginally outside it (observed: Plaza Eliptica at 40.38460, ~44 m outside). A strict envelope check would fail a healthy build.

madrid_city_and_surroundings_feed_area.note: INTEGRITY ENVELOPE ONLY for the Madrid Destino / esmadrid accommodation feed - not a statement of coverage. The dataset is published as 'Alojamientos de la ciudad de Madrid' and its specification describes the content as accommodation of 'la ciudad de Madrid y alrededores' (the city of Madrid and its surroundings). The box is deliberately loose so that a record in the surroundings does not fail the build, while a null-island coordinate, a swapped lat/lon or a different country still does. On 2026-09-29, 4 of 613 records fell outside the municipality, the furthest at 40.711 N / -3.994 E; those records are reported as a manifest warning against madrid_city_area and are deliberately NOT filtered here, because narrowing the layer would be an analytical semantics change rather than an integrity fix.
madrid_city_and_surroundings_feed_area.not_a_regional_dataset: This envelope must never be read as Comunidad de Madrid coverage. This feed is a city-and-surroundings accommodation register, not a regional one. A future Comunidad de Madrid level requires its own authoritative regional datasets and must not inherit this feed as a proxy for them.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: Accommodation listings curated and published by Madrid Destino / esMADRID, taken as a deployment snapshot of the published XML catalogue and counted one per listing. This is a tourism-promotion catalogue, NOT a complete administrative register of accommodation. It is NOT accommodation capacity, beds, places or rooms (a 300-room hotel and a 4-room pension each count as one); NOT occupancy, price or legal status; NOT the complete municipal accommodation stock and NOT regional stock. Its catalogue universe is heterogeneous and includes objects such as university residences and campsites. Published as 'Alojamientos de la ciudad de Madrid', covering the city of Madrid and its surroundings, so it is neither a strictly municipal register nor a Comunidad de Madrid one, and must not be used as a regional dataset. See docs/ACCOMMODATION_NUMERATOR_AUDIT.md (Gate A).

sources.source_period_semantics: No effective or edition date of the geometry is published, so this geography has no source period; source_period is null and source_period_known is false. What the authority does publish is a dataset version ('Versión de los datos'): district v3.2.1 and barrio v3.4.1 at capture, recorded in geography/madrid_admin.meta.json under source_version.datasets[*].published_version. sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING since the Area Profile feature: the application now resolves each Lens centre to its official barrio and district at runtime and names that place in the interface, so this artifact is consumed by a user-facing feature. The Node and Python test suites still enforce the same structural contract on every push; this gate is the second line, at publication.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: Administrative reference geography for spatial joins and containment only. It is a common join target for future datasets (Padron, accommodation, VUT, restaurants, housing, socioeconomic and environmental indicators), not an analytical metric and not a denominator on its own. The municipality polygon is DERIVED as the union of the 21 official district polygons and is flagged as such. Administrative-area statistics must never be spatially distributed into a circular Lens or any sub-area; a Lens may report the official barrio/district containing a point, kept clearly separate from circle-derived measurements. This municipal geography is not Comunidad de Madrid geography.

sources.source_period_semantics: The population period is the source reference date, published as '1 de enero de <year>' (a real Padron reference date), recorded in population/madrid_population.json under source_period.reference_date and echoed in the sidecar meta. It is source-derived and never taken from the build clock; the builder's retrieval/build time is recorded separately as retrieved_at in the meta. The selected period is the latest annual reference date whose barrio coverage exactly matches the canonical geography, so a year with partial coverage is treated as incomplete rather than as the latest. The geography version this joins against (barrio v3.4.1 / district v3.2.1) is recorded in the meta under geography_linkage and is distinct from the population period: an audit can state 'population period X joined to Madrid barrio geography v3.4.1'.

sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING since the Area Profile feature: the application now reads the registered-resident figure of the barrio containing a Lens centre and shows it, with its reference date, in the interface. A deployment must not publish a resident count that is missing, mis-joined or detached from its period. The UI abstains rather than showing a zero when a figure is absent, but an artifact that is broken at build time must not reach the public site at all. The Node and Python test suites still enforce the same contract on every push.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: Persons registered in the municipal Padron for the reference date. This is a residential denominator only: it is NOT people physically present at a given moment, NOT daytime population, NOT tourists, NOT workers present, NOT unique mobile-device users, NOT households and NOT housing units. This PR defines no tourism indicator, no accommodation-per-resident or hotels-per-1000 ratio, no tourism pressure and no composite score. A barrio population belongs to the whole official barrio and must never be spatially distributed into a circular Lens; a Lens may state 'the centre is in barrio X, which has Y registered residents for period Z', where Y remains a barrio statistic, not the population inside the circle. This municipal population is not Comunidad de Madrid population.

sources.source_period_semantics: The source declares NO reference date and NO effective date, so this layer has no source period: source_period is null and source_period_known is false. Four different dates exist around this artifact and are never collapsed into one. (1) The HTTP Last-Modified header observed on the resource file when the builder fetched it (Mon, 07 Sep 2026 10:11:03 GMT), recorded in the artifact under source_state.xlsx_http_last_modified. It describes the state of the FILE SERVED and is NOT a publisher-declared publication, effective or reference date; it must never be presented as one, and the interface says 'source file state', never 'reference'. (2) The span of per-record licence grant dates present in the extract (2019-03-06 to 2026-09-02), which is a property of the records, not of the publication. (3) The portal catalogue's own metadata date. (4) The builder's retrieved_at clock. The residential denominator's reference date (1 January 2026) belongs to a DIFFERENT source with different temporal semantics and the two are never shown as one shared period.

count_fields.note: COUNT of distinct EXPEDIENTE_LU and SUM of the source column 'N VUT' respectively. A licence is not a dwelling: in the audited extract one licence covered 48 units, so vut_units >= vut_licences must hold for every record and the two are never given each other's name. The user-facing primary quantity is vut_units.

expected_counts.note: Every canonical barrio must carry exactly one pair of counts for this source snapshot; district and municipality totals are derived from the barrios. A change to these counts is a change to the canonical join universe and must not reach a deployment unnoticed.

expected_source_totals.note: The totals of THIS COMMITTED SNAPSHOT, pinned so an accidental or partial regeneration is a visible diff rather than a silent one. They are not eternal source truths: the upstream dataset is updated bimonthly, and a deliberate refresh re-runs scripts/build_vut_licence_numerator.py and updates these numbers in the same reviewed pull request as the artifact. The builder derives them from the source and never reads them from here.

sources.zero_semantics: Scoped to this source extract only. The extract enumerates granted activity-licence records across the whole municipality, so a barrio with no matched record carries zero published granted licences and zero source-reported units rather than missing data. This is the one documented exception to this project's 'missing is not zero' rule. A zero is NOT an assertion that no tourist-dwelling activity has ever existed or exists today in that barrio, and a failure to load or validate this artifact must never be degraded into a zero: the interface abstains instead.
sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING since the Area Profile feature began showing licensed VUT context: the application reads the licensed-VUT figures of the barrio containing a Lens centre and displays them, with a descriptive per-1,000-registered-residents ratio, in the interface. A deployment must not publish an administrative indicator that is missing, mis-joined, numerically incoherent or detached from its provenance, because the failure mode is a confident wrong number - or a plausible-looking zero - rather than a visibly empty panel. The browser degrades gracefully when a runtime fetch fails and shows the licensed-VUT block as unavailable; that is a separate concern from this gate, which verifies the COMMITTED artifact at publication time. The Node and Python suites enforce the same contract on every push.
sources.deployment_source_role: COMMITTED ADMINISTRATIVE SNAPSHOT. This artifact is not rebuilt during the Pages deployment (rebuilt_at_deploy is false): deployment validation verifies the committed file, and a successful deployment therefore does NOT mean the upstream source was re-fetched at deploy time. Refreshing it requires explicitly re-running scripts/build_vut_licence_numerator.py and reviewing the diff, including the pinned expected_source_totals above. Nothing about this layer is live data.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: A count of urban-planning activity licences GRANTED for tourist-dwelling (vivienda de uso turistico) use in the city of Madrid, and of the tourist-dwelling units those licences include. The primary quantity is units; the licence count is supporting evidence and a licence is NOT a dwelling. It does NOT establish that the dwellings are currently operating: the source carries no revocation, expiry or cessation field and publishes no retention policy, so nothing may call these 'active', 'operating' or 'current' tourist dwellings, and the extract is not described as a cumulative stock. It is NOT all VUT (it excludes responsible declarations filed with the Comunidad de Madrid and the regional inventory), NOT all accommodation (the publisher names tourist apartments, hostels, guest houses, hotels, pensions and aparthotels as excluded), NOT beds, rooms or places, NOT platform listings and NOT evidence of the legality of any platform listing. It is NOT a measure of tourism pressure, overtourism, saturation, carrying capacity, tourism intensity, resident displacement, neighbourhood burden, impact or attractiveness, and it is never ranked, banded, scored or mapped as a heat surface. The per-1,000-registered-residents figure is a DESCRIPTIVE ratio of two administrative facts with two different periods, not a rate of anything and not a share of dwellings: the denominator is registered residents, never homes or households. Counts belong to the WHOLE OFFICIAL BARRIO and must never be spatially distributed into a circular Lens or any sub-area.

sources.freshness_evidence: reference_date is the latest observation month in the committed series, 2026-08 (ISO month; month precision preserved, never promoted to a day). source_state PROVISIONAL: INE publishes this reference month provisionally (FK_TipoDato; months of the current statistical year are provisional and revised later). update_frequency MONTHLY is INE's monthly EOH operation cadence. published_at is null: INE's publication calendar ('around day 23 of the following month') is a calendar, not a declared edition date, and is never inferred into published_at. retrieved_at is destination/madrid_hotel_demand.meta.json retrieved_at. scope MUNICIPALITY: the figure describes the whole municipality (28079) and never a district, barrio or Lens circle.
sources.authority: Instituto Nacional de Estadistica (INE) - Encuesta de Ocupacion Hotelera
sources.spatial_scope_note: DELIBERATELY NULL. Every other source in this registry is a set of located records or an administrative area, so a bounding box is a meaningful integrity check on it. This source has no coordinates at all: it is one citywide monthly figure for the municipality of Madrid. A spatial envelope would imply a geometry the source does not have. What replaces it is the municipality-code check below.
sources.expected_operation_note: The INE statistical operation this series MUST come from: Encuesta de Ocupacion Hotelera. Operation identity is the central protection against the operation-239 name collision described in series_codes below, so the committed sidecar's declared statistical_operation is verified against this value at the deployment gate and a disagreement blocks publication.
sources.geography_semantics: The official INE 'punto turistico' named Madrid. INE's own EOH methodology (edition 2025, section 5.12) defines a punto turistico as 'Municipio donde la concentracion de la oferta turistica es significativa' - a MUNICIPALITY - and section 5.13 defines a 'zona turistica' separately as a set of municipalities, so the two cannot be confused. INE's Tempus3 metadata for variable 103 (PUNTOS TURISTICOS) under operation 238 publishes the value 'Madrid' with Codigo 28079, the official municipality code, which is the same code carried by the canonical geography artifact. The figure therefore describes the WHOLE MUNICIPALITY and no part of it: not a district, not a barrio, not a Lens circle.
sources.source_period_semantics: Each observation describes a CALENDAR MONTH, and the artifact stores that month as its period. Four different dates exist around this artifact and are never collapsed into one. (1) The month an observation describes. (2) Whether that month is Definitivo or Provisional, which the source publishes per observation as FK_TipoDato and which this project stores as 'status'; months of the current statistical year are provisional and are revised later. (3) INE's publication calendar - the methodology states provisional results for a reference month appear around day 23 of the following month. (4) The builder's retrieved_at clock, which is when this snapshot was taken and is not a property of the data. The interface shows the OBSERVATION PERIOD prominently and keeps retrieval in the source disclosure.

series_codes.note: Series are selected by CODE and each one's own FK_Operacion is verified to be 238 before use. They are NEVER selected by name: statistical operation 239 (Encuesta de Ocupacion en Apartamentos Turisticos) publishes series with IDENTICAL names through the same tourist-point dimension. EOT2743 (operation 238, hotels) and EOT9411 (operation 239, tourist apartments) are both named 'Nacional. Viajeros. Madrid. Residentes en Espana.' and reported 320,715 and 21,334 for their latest published month. Operation 180 (Indicadores de Rentabilidad del Sector Hotelero) supplies ADR and RevPAR through the same dimension and is likewise excluded.

sources.totals_are_published_not_derived: The travellers and overnight-stays totals are read from source-published series and are NEVER computed by adding the two residence components. The published total and that sum disagree by +/-1 in 32 of 105 traveller periods and 26 of 105 overnight-stay periods, because the publisher rounds each estimate independently, so summing would publish a number the source does not publish. The composition block is the one place the two components are added, because a displayed share must total 100 per cent, and that denominator is documented as the sum of the components rather than the published total.

expected_counts.note: ENGINEERING guardrail against an ingestion collapse, not an analytical threshold. The committed series runs 2018-01 to 2026-08. It grows by one month per publication, so a floor well below the observed length passes legitimate growth and fails a truncated download.

sources.zero_semantics: Scoped to this published series. The source published an explicit 0 for 2020-04, when hotels were closed under the COVID-19 state of alarm, and that zero is a real published observation rather than missing data. It is kept distinct from 2020-05 and 2020-06, which the source published as NULL with the note 'Dato no disponible por cierre debido a crisis COVID19'. A null is never rendered as a zero, never interpolated and never averaged over, and a failure to load or validate this artifact must never be degraded into a zero: the interface abstains instead.
sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING because the Destination Context surface publishes these figures as user-facing numbers with a year-over-year comparison. A deployment must not publish an official statistic that is missing, mis-parsed, detached from its provenance or - the worst case - drawn from the wrong statistical operation, because the failure mode is a confident wrong number under a correct-looking label rather than a visibly empty panel. The browser degrades gracefully when a runtime fetch fails and shows Destination Context as unavailable while leaving the Area Profile, the Lens metrics, VUT and HATI untouched; that is a separate concern from this gate, which verifies the COMMITTED artifact at publication time.
sources.deployment_source_role: COMMITTED STATISTICAL SNAPSHOT. This artifact is not rebuilt during the Pages deployment (rebuilt_at_deploy is false): deployment validation verifies the committed file, and a successful deployment therefore does NOT mean the publisher was re-queried at deploy time. Refreshing it requires explicitly re-running scripts/build_destination_context.py and reviewing the diff. Nothing about this layer is live data, and the browser never calls the publisher's API at runtime.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: Hotel-sector demand in the municipality of Madrid, as measured by the official INE hotel occupancy survey. 'Travellers' is the survey's viajeros entrados: persons making one or more consecutive overnight stays in the SAME establishment, so a person staying in two hotels is counted twice - it is NOT a count of unique people and NOT a count of visitors to Madrid. 'Overnight stays' is pernoctaciones, each night a traveller is accommodated. This is NOT total tourism demand, NOT all accommodation and NOT all visitors: it excludes tourist apartments, tourist dwellings (VUT), campsites, rural accommodation, day visitors and everyone staying in unpaid or private accommodation. The residence split is the publisher's own 'Residentes en Espana' / 'Residentes en el extranjero', which is PLACE OF RESIDENCE and must never be relabelled as domestic/international tourists, nationality or trip type. It is NOT a measure of tourism pressure, overtourism, saturation, carrying capacity, tourism intensity or attractiveness, it is never ranked, banded or scored, and it carries no explanation of why a figure changed: the product reports the observation and never attributes it to events, weather, prices or policy. The figure belongs to the WHOLE MUNICIPALITY and must never be distributed into a district, a barrio or a Lens circle.

sources.freshness_evidence: reference_date is the latest source month 2026-07 (meta temporal_contract.latest_source_month; ISO month). retrieved_at is the meta retrieved_at. sources.source_period_semantics: Each record is a crossing in the monthly worksheet named by source_month. Every sheet year must match the declared workbook year; the workbook year is only an acquisition container and retrieved_at is kept separately.
sources.source_universe: Residents in Spain travelling to a province different from their province of residence, disaggregated by origin and destination municipality. Same-province travel, including travel within Madrid province, is outside this statistic's universe.
sources.suppression_rule: Only origin-destination crossings with more than 30 tourists are published. Origins may be outside the source universe; within the universe, absent origins are not zero and no residual or all-origin share may be created.

It catches a truncated workbook, broken Madrid filter or incomplete parser without rejecting a legitimate early-year workbook with only one or two available monthly sheets.

Same-province travel, including travel within Madrid province, is outside the statistic's universe. Descriptive context, not a complete distribution of domestic tourism, an all-origin share, a market attractiveness ranking, causal evidence, forecast, barrio, district or Lens-circle measure. expected_counts.note: The official layer is a MIXED UNIVERSE and the raw feature count is NOT a count of planning ambitos; the phrase '765 ambitos' is prohibited wording. The builder classifies every record by its exact official code, keeps only the ambito-like universe and FAILS the build on a code it cannot classify, so no record is ever silently discarded or silently admitted. These counts are pinned observations of the calibration run: a change in the official universe must be a visible diff in a reviewed pull request.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: An ENGINEERING guardrail against an ingestion collapse (a truncated response, a schema change, an upstream outage that still returns parseable GeoJSON), set far below the observed count. It is not an analytical threshold and not a claim about how many planning ambitos Madrid has.

sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING from the moment K6 (#68) began resolving each Lens centre to its containing official planning ambito and naming that ambito, with its exact official code, in the interface. sources.interpretation_ceiling: Official planning-ámbito boundaries and codes as published by the Ayuntamiento de Madrid. sources.freshness_evidence: K6 current-edition reference_date 2026-01-01 is stated inside each selected source file. K7 separately compares the source-stated 2025-07-01 and 2026-01-01 editions, each with its own resource identity and full fingerprint in change_detection.editions. editions.selection_rule: The newest STATED REFERENCE DATE within the current schema era. Never by resource id, resource name, filename or catalogue position: the id order is not chronological (203200-15 is Enero 2026 while 203200-16 is Enero 2025), so selecting by id returns the wrong edition.
editions.note: K6 keeps one current edition per family as its primary evidence. K7 stores a separate, fixed comparison pair: the source-stated 2025-07-01 and 2026-01-01 editions. The pair is selected by reference date plus full SHA-256, and does not mutate the K6 current-edition object. A later edition requires an independent comparability gate before any pair change.

sources.source_period_semantics: K6 current evidence has the source-stated reference date 2026-01-01. K7 compares exactly two source-stated tabular editions, 2025-07-01 and 2026-01-01, within the current S1_FOUR_PHASE_FLAT and S2_SPLIT_RESIDENTIAL_FLAT schema eras. The K7 surface shows both dates. Where the K2 rail requires one date, it applies the existing oldest-contributor rule and uses 2025-07-01. Each edition separately records its source URL, resource identity, full fingerprint, schema era and retrieval provenance. Geometry is a separate source with no declared date.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: ENGINEERING guardrails against an ingestion collapse, set far below the observed counts. Not analytical thresholds and not claims about how many ambitos are under development. The buildability family publishes more ROWS than distinct codes because it reports buildability according to the ambito's situacion; those rows are preserved separately and never summed.

expected_joins.note: Exact-identifier joins against the committed geometry universe, reproducing the Gate L section 17 baseline (S1 666/667, S2 230/230). A -RP suffix is NEVER stripped: it marks a distinct Revision Parcial ambito, and Gate L measured that normalising codes REDUCES exact matches. Unmatched records are reported in the meta sidecar's joins block, never dropped: an ambito with geometry but no published row keeps an explicit NOT_PUBLISHED_IN_EDITION state.

published_fields.no_scalar_stage: The four phase columns are FOUR INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED FIELDS. Gate L section 12 measured them as multi-dimensional (empirically non-funnel) and the publisher documents no ordering, so no overall stage, stage number, progression, percentage, completion, advancement, delay or timeline exists in the artifact, the model or the interface.
published_fields.excluded_columns_reason: Gate L §16 measured these values as exactly residential buildability ÷ 100, with fractional results, at a match rate of 1.0 across every row. They are a mechanical m²/100 proxy at an assumed 100 m² per dwelling, not a count of dwelling units, and no protected-housing count column exists. The product publishes buildability in m² only and exposes no dwelling count.

sources.zero_semantics: The edition itself distinguishes a blank cell from a published 0, and so does this layer: a blank buildability cell is NOT_PUBLISHED with a null value, and a published 0 is a real zero meaning the edition publishes no available buildability of that use class for that ambito. Neither is ever substituted for the other, nothing falls back to 0, and an ambito the edition carries no row for is NOT_PUBLISHED_IN_EDITION rather than zero. A published 0 is NOT an assertion that nothing can ever be built there: it is what the selected edition publishes for that use class, under that situacion, on its stated reference date.
sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING from the moment K6 (#68) began publishing the four official development-phase values and available buildability in m2 edificable to the reader. A deployment must not publish official planning evidence that is missing, mis-joined, schema-drifted or detached from its edition identity, because the failure mode is a confident wrong state - or a plausible-looking zero where the publisher published nothing - rather than a visibly empty panel. The browser degrades to explicit unavailable states when a runtime fetch fails; that is a separate concern from this gate, which verifies the COMMITTED artifact at publication time.
sources.deployment_source_role: COMMITTED EDITION SNAPSHOT. Not rebuilt during the Pages deployment (rebuilt_at_deploy is false): a successful deployment does NOT mean the official editions were re-fetched. Refreshing requires re-running scripts/build_ambito_development_state.py - which re-resolves the catalogue, re-selects by stated reference date and FAILS on schema drift rather than shifting a column - and reviewing the diff, including the pinned edition identities above.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: Four INDEPENDENT published administrative development-phase values per planning ámbito, and available planning buildability (edificabilidad disponible) by use class in m² edificable, as published in ONE dated edition of each official family. The four phase fields do NOT form one overall completion stage: they are multi-dimensional, the publisher documents no ordering, and no stage, stage number, progression, percentage, completion, advancement, delay or timeline is derivable from them. A published phase state is an ADMINISTRATIVE state, never proof of physical construction progress (PLANNING_STATE_TRANSITION != PHYSICAL_URBAN_CHANGE). 'No Necesita' is a distinct published value whose precise meaning the audited documentation does not define; it does not mean not applicable, skipped, complete, zero or unavailable. 'PGOUM-85' and 'PGOUM-97' are plan-of-origin markers occupying phase cells, not progress states. Available buildability is what the plan makes available, NOT what remains to be physically built and NOT an estimate of what will be built. NO dwelling count is published or derivable: the source's Nº Viviendas columns are residential buildability ÷ 100 with fractional values and are excluded. Every figure describes the WHOLE ámbito and is never apportioned into a Lens circle, a barrio or any sub-area, and never combined with a value of another analytical scope. K6 shows one current edition per family. K7 separately compares the pinned 2025-07-01 and 2026-01-01 tabular editions within the matching current schema eras; the comparison does not cover geometry. Geometry and identifiers come through a separate official route; every quantity and state here comes from the dated CC BY 4.0 editions.

change_detection.comparison_basis: Two explicitly named editions selected by source-stated reference date plus full SHA-256; comparison is within one schema era. Entity identity is {edition}:{exact_code}.

absence_reason_reference.title: Ámbitos del PGOUM que no son objeto de seguimiento
absence_reason_reference.matching_rule: Attach a documented reason only to its exact published code; do not infer one from a prefix, name or near-code match.

change_detection.absence_reason_policy: ABSENT_FROM_EDITION remains the primary outcome. Each record carries SOURCE_DOCUMENTED only with an exact-code annex reason; otherwise it carries CAUSE_UNRESOLVED.

sources.freshness_evidence: retrieved_at is the crosswalk's generated_at (callejero/madrid_ndp_crosswalk.meta.json). The bulk Callejero Oficial publishes NO reference_date and NO published_at, so both are explicit nulls: the dated filename, the HTTP Last-Modified header, the weekly cadence and the retrieval clock are observed resource state only (recorded under sources.*.observed_resource_state) and none is promoted into a source reference date. update_frequency WEEKLY is the callejero bulk cadence. No definitive/provisional status is published. scope ADDRESS_POINT: each resolved record locates one official address point.
sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - CADMA / Callejero Oficial
sources.source_period_semantics: The crosswalk has no source period: the callejero publishes none and the licence register publishes none. Its generated_at is the build/retrieval time, recorded as retrieved_at, never as a reference date. The dated callejero filenames and HTTP validators are observed resource state in the meta and are never collapsed into a publication date.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: Ingestion-collapse guardrails, not analytical thresholds. The match-rate floor (0.90) sits ~8 points below the pinned Gate M row rate (0.9797) and below the lowest observed per-year rate (0.9733), so a legitimate small source update passes while a gross collapse (callejero truncated or unreachable) fails. The historical-recovery floor (20, baseline 86) is a SEPARATE guard: it catches a regression where the builder silently stops using the historical callejero and the ~86 recovered rows fall toward zero. Changing a floor is a visible diff justified in its pull request.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: An administrative ADDRESS_POINT crosswalk resolving the granted-licence NDP set to an official callejero location. A resolved coordinate is where the official callejero places an address; it is NOT evidence that any work occurred there. Resolution may be CURRENT (the callejero's own official barrio code) or HISTORICAL (a dated historical version selected by the licence grant date, with a POLYGON-DERIVED barrio from the official historical coordinate); the two barrio provenances are kept distinct and never presented as identical. Unresolved rows are withheld and reported, never geocoded externally or approximated. It is a reference crosswalk, never a count of anything.

sources.freshness_evidence: retrieved_at is the artifact generated_at (planning/madrid_urban_licences.meta.json). The granted-licence register publishes NO reference_date and NO published_at, so both are explicit nulls: the monthly cadence, the HTTP Last-Modified header and the retrieval clock are observed resource state only and none is promoted into a source reference date. The per-record grant-date span (date_extent) is a property of the records, not a publication date. update_frequency MONTHLY is the publisher-declared cadence. No definitive/provisional status is published. scope ADDRESS_POINT: counts are records spatially included in a Lens circle, never a barrio-level figure.
sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Agencia de Actividades / Direccion General de Control de la Edificacion
sources.source_period_semantics: The register declares no reference or effective date, so this layer has no source period: source_period stays null. The grant-date extent (2023-01-13..2026-09-30 at calibration) is a property of the records and bounds the user date window; it is never a publication date. The crosswalk's callejero resources keep their own freshness and are never collapsed into this layer's date.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: Ingestion-collapse guardrails, not analytical thresholds. Each family floor sits well below its pinned Gate M count so churn passes and a family vanishing fails; the resolved-rows and match-rate floors catch a join collapse; the historical-recovery floor catches the historical route silently disappearing.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: A count of granted administrative urban licences spatially included in the Lens circle (scope ADDRESS_POINT), by family and grant-date window. GRANTED-ONLY: the register is RESOLUCION=Conceder, so there is no applications/refusals denominator and NO approval rate, rejection rate, refusal count or success rate exists. A granted licence is NOT evidence that work started, construction occurred or completed, occupancy happened, or the permitted quantity was built: granted is not built. The three families (building/urbanistic, activity, temporary activity) are NOT one homogeneous universe and are NEVER summed into a single cross-family total. The mapped layer is the RESOLVED SUBSET of the register; unresolved rows are reported in the coverage metadata and never dropped from the denominator. The crosswalk may resolve via current or historical official callejero, with distinct current/historical administrative-geography provenance. Licence records may concern places also present in Censo de Locales, licensed VUT or hospitality/activity evidence; these universes are NEVER summed as unique businesses or sites. Counts are ADDRESS_POINT records and are never converted into a barrio-level figure, ranked by barrio or district, or rendered as a density, heatmap or choropleth surface. Responsible declarations (dataset 133556) are not ingested.
